sources.title: Cancellieri and Marchi van Cauwelaert: medieval Corsica and Genoese colonisation
sources.note: 2023 scholarly volume, chapter printed pp. 101 to 123, especially 103 to 107. Full PDF inspected. One conservative budget for entire volume.

sources.title: Vannina Marchi van Cauwelaert: the territorial policy of San Giorgio in Corsica
sources.note: 2009 primary archival research, printed p. 437 directly accessible; trade, competing power and late-fifteenth-century urbanisation.

sources.title: Antoine-Marie Graziani: ruptures and continuities in San Giorgio government
sources.note: 2006 primary archival research, printed p. 76 / PDF index 2. Contract taxation and local civil justice; do not project later sixteenth-century staff details backward.

sources.title: Daniel Istria: excavation of Cotone, or Paese Vecchio, Bastia
sources.note: 1993 excavation report published online 2019; paragraphs 1 to 6. Proposed upper floors and oven functions are explicitly qualified.

sources.title: Antoine Albitreccia: Bonifacio and its water supply
sources.note: 1940 geographical and architectural study, printed p. 40. Original indexed page directly supports thirteenth-century municipal cistern, roof collection, 650 cubic metres and access through porch pillars. Direct page fetch errored; indexed primary text inspected.

sources.title: Mairie de Bonifacio: Saint-François church and convent
sources.note: Municipal monument history; late-thirteenth-century Franciscan presence and 1398 well by Abrigho de Pistoïa. Speculative bathing function omitted.

sources.title: Jean Chiorboli: Corsicans faithful to the Republic of Genoa
sources.note: Linguist’s primary onomastic analysis in ICN, 7 April 2023, printed p. 20 / PDF index 19. Reproduces Latinised name from the 1453 oath list published in the 1881 historical-society bulletin. It is a scholarly transcription, not direct manuscript inspection.

sources.title: Italian State Archives SIAS: Magistrato di Corsica
sources.note: Official archival authority record; San Giorgio first granted Corsica in 1453 and new magistracy established in 1562 when the island returned to direct republican administration. Indexed original inspected.

sources.title: Polybius: Histories, book 4, the war among Cretan cities
sources.note: Primary ancient narrative in Evelyn Shuckburgh’s English translation; sections 53 to 55, PDF indices 39 to 40. Author’s hostile generalisations about Cretans are not adopted.

sources.title: Greek cultural heritage service: Lato archaeological guide
sources.note: Official bilingual guide, PDF indices 1 to 2, visible fourth-/third-century city, residential terraces, public cistern and dining complex.

sources.title: Diazoma and the 24th Ephorate: gathering spaces at Lato
sources.note: Monument record with Ministry/Ephorate documentation: staircase about eighty seats, civic and religious gatherings; separate theatre date uncertain.

sources.title: Niki Tsatsaki: residences and workshops at Nissi-Eleutherna
sources.note: Primary University of Crete excavation research, printed pp. 67 to 71, especially 68 to 69. House A begins in third century BCE; pottery repair and manufacture, cereals and many domestic assemblages belong to late-second-/early-first-century second phase. Those later examples explicitly labelled in prose.

sources.title: Ruth Westgate: house and society in Classical and Hellenistic Crete
sources.note: Author’s 2007 research abstract, accessible directly. Differences at Lato/Trypetos and cautious proposal about women’s access to domestic space; not proof of equality or a universal Cretan pattern.

sources.title: Heraklion Archaeological Museum: decree honouring Patroklos
sources.note: Museum object E213, Hellenistic period, translation of council/assembly decree for Macedonian Patroklos sent by King Ptolemy. Indexed original inspected; direct fetch failed. No exact decree year supplied here.

sources.title: Practicalities of Hellenistic Ruler Cults: the Itanos reservoir dedication
sources.note: PHRC015, IC III iv 18, Heraklion Museum E64, dated 220 to 209 BCE. Complete stone; Greek edition line 3 and English translation directly inspected. Sample uses editorial accents and word division, not a claim of facsimile capitals.

sources.title: École française d’Athènes: Itanos survey and fortifications
sources.note: Don Evely report based on 2010 archaeological publication. Southwest tower architectural date mid-fourth to mid-third century BCE; Ptolemaic attribution is tentative. Eight surveyed towers overlook sea and central plain; avoid claiming all share this date.

sources.title: Ashmolean Museum: myths of the labyrinth and a Hellenistic Knossian coin
sources.note: Museum coin HCR 4579, 300 to 200 BCE; labyrinth design. Same page provides Roman conquest beginning in 69 BCE and later Gortyn capital, used for ending without insisting on a disputed exact completion year.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Imported whole-island geometry at 1000, 1100, 1200, 1279, 1300 and 1400 is a regional envelope, not evidence for continuous unified government. Narrative excludes the eighteenth-century Paoli republic. 1492 is coverage only. Latinised oath-list sample is explicitly a modern scholarly transcription of a medieval record.

Imported geometry at -300 covers the entire island; index coverage -300 to -200. Use regional Hellenistic narrative, not Minoan civilisation or island-wide monarchy. House A’s pottery-workshop evidence explicitly dated later than map century. Reservoir sample is contemporary Greek inscription in scholarly transcription. 200 BCE is not an ending date.
